title: Project SunFlower - Capital A x Steinreich Communications group

sentences.text: Hi Stan, how you doing?
Good.
How are you, Andrew?
Yeah, I'm good, thank you.
I'm good.
Whereabouts are you calling from?
So I am at a conference in Orlando.
How about yourself?
I'm in Somerset in the uk so not quite as sunny as Florida, but good.
What kind of conference is it?
So we're in the US we're actually the largest home.
Well, our practice, we have a practice in home furnishings.
So this is a betting industry conference and we represent in that category six of the top 10 players in that category.
Wow.
Yeah, that's pretty impressive.
So tell me, tell me a little bit about your business.
I'm not familiar with your agency.
Yeah, sure.
So we are, we're Capital A.
So we're a mergers and acquisitions advisory and we exclusively work in in marketing services.
So all of our clients are either buying and selling marketing services businesses.
We work on the, the sell side.
We have a platform Agencies co, which is a marketplace for agency sellers.

And also as Capital A, we work on the buy side working with either high scale marketing agencies or agency groups and also with private equity and private investors as well, helping them to find businesses to acquire and then helping them in the entire process.
So we get to see both sides of the table working on, on deals in all sorts of ways.
But it's all marketing services.
So everybody pretty much who's a client is usually a marketing agency owner themselves.
And how long have you been in this business?
Nine years.
I've been working in M and A exclusively but prior to that I actually had a fairly large digital marketing and media business in the UK which I actually sold to private equity.

So I've come out of that with my own experience and really I kind of look to work with the founders and help them bridge the gap between the sort of financial, more financial side and the creative side.
Got it.
We've worked with Art Stevens and the Stevens Group, if that's familiar to you at all over the years.
We've done a couple of acquisitions already historically.
Let me tell you a little bit about us so you have some context.

Actually July will be our 22nd year in business and my background, former New York Times reporter, worked for ABC News as a producer and then went over to the deep dark other side and was at Burson, Marsteller, Fleischmann, Hillard and Edelman.
I ran different business units and geographies for them over about a 20 year period and then decided if I'm busy selling and running businesses for other people, I might as well try this myself.
And that's where that bright idea came from.
And I still have hair on my head a little bit, so I guess it's worked.
And look, today we're public relations.
We obviously are doing social media as well.
Clients, you know, we do, you know, some advertising work really as a service, you know, to our clients.
It's not a main line of business for us.
We have nine offices around the world.
We have 110 people.
The offices are small around the world and that's really designed on purpose.
It's mainly facilitate export business, you know, and typically globally it's multi local multinationals who want to market into the United States.
Primarily, you know, home furnishings for us is about and consumer products about 30% of our business.
But we're fairly integrated.
So we also do financial services, professional services, high tech, travel and tourism and a fair amount of government work around the world as well.
So that's a little bit of an overview on the side.
Yeah, fantastic.
Okay, so.
So our client, as you'll know from the im, is based on the coast of Georgia and it's a, you know, relatively small PR firm headed up.

Actually she's British, the lady that owns them and runs the business currently, but has previously been exceedingly successful in the UK before she relocated to the US with her husband, who's American.
She actually sold a company, a PR company in the UK which was quite well known and is now part of Omnicom, I think.
So it has continued after her.
And this is not so much a retirement sale, but she is certainly heading in that direction.
So it's a legacy sale of sorts.
She's not looking to get out anytime soon and with the right buyer, she could stay for a long time.
She's in her late 50s, but she has a great team and they've got great experience, particularly in the government and nonprofit sectors.
So I think there's possibly a good match for you there.
And she also does some other stuff, some local business and some education and some of the local cities as well, they represent them, PR and stuff like that.
So it could be a really good fit.
And really the nature of these calls is kind of when we come across a buyer that we've never met before is to make sure that you exist.
Because obviously we get.
I'm not an avatar, I'm not an avatar.
Exactly.
We could be a very good AI.
But obviously, as you can imagine, we get a lot of tire kickers.
So really our job is to make sure that, that you do exist and that you have a strategy for the acquisition.
If it was to go forward.
So, yeah, it sounds like you guys are extremely experienced and relatively large as well, if you're able to open up offices across the globe.
So really our concern is just to make sure that the organization is big enough or is cohesive enough to be able to take on an acquisition, even though this is relatively a small one as well.
Right.
So look, I mean, I'll tell you generally because, I mean, it's good for us to know one another based on the business in any way.
We typically look for under a million dollar companies.
Okay.
And I'll tell you that I sort of like that zone.
You know, it's fraught with a little bit of terror because you never quite know what you're buying, you know, when they're that small.
But, you know, it, it.

It tends to work well for us when there's a strong, you know, leader, but there's also a strong number two, you know, because we've also had some bad experience where there's only been a leader and no number two, and we've done an acquisition and it's kind of fizzled when the owner left, you know, of course.
Yeah.
So I'm looking to avoid that.
And obviously also just that there's some synergy in the team where they can do, you know, so really, when I.

When I asked you for the P and L, and I understand all the reasons why you didn't want to send that, that really kind of gets us into the guts of what the business looks like and, and how it operates.
And that for me is important, you know, likewise.
You know, as I said, we work with the Stevens Group.
We get a fair amount of, you know, incoming opportunity from him.
But what I've learned over the years is that we really want to take a look a little deeper before we engage and waste the owner's time or waste our own time in terms of looking at a business.
Yeah, well, I guess we're seeing it from the other side then, Stan.

So from our point of view, what we don't want to do is start lifting up the kimono with all this of the financial side of things before our client in particular has had a chance to see if there is any chemistry, because for them, it's extremely personal process where they're giving away the fine details of their business.
So it's kind of six of one and a half dozen the other.
I understand your reason, but in terms of our client, they just want half an hour of your time to see if there's a fit and that there's a big vision for them to be part of.
And if you're able to have that quick chat with them, they.
Then she will be more than happy to reveal everything about the business because her hope will be that there is chemistry and that you'll be happy to make an offer if you can get into the financials.
And that's kind of our approach, really.
Sure.
So look, schedule wise, it's tight on the next couple of weeks, but I will have a window Thursday morning of this week.
Okay.
If that works for her.
What time zone are you in, Stan?
Some.
I'll be east coast.
I'll be in New Jersey in the, in the morning.
So I would say that from about 10, 10 to noon would be ideal if she can do it on Thursday.
If not, I.
I'm sure we can find time next week.
I just can't commit because I've got two competing trips at the moment.
So right now I'm planning to be in Washington, in Germany next week, but we have a major pitch going on in Israel that I may pop into.
And it ain't so easy getting in and out of Israel these days.
So that's my.
So.
So my point is next week, I'm sure we can find time.
I just can't give you a commitment to next week at this point.
Well, I think Leslie will be extremely keen to give you half an hour of your time if she can get it.
Obviously she's, she's very keen to meet people in the process that are looking to speak to her about business.
So, yeah, if, if we can.
If we cannot get that set up, then of course, let's see how flexible you can be after the two week traveling all over the globe by the sounds of it.
But, but I think tomorrow she will probably pull something out that.
Sorry, it's not tomorrow, it's a day after tomorrow.
She'll pull something out of the hat to get some time with you.
So let's get that set up.
I've.
I've put that window into my calendar.
I will jump on a call with Leslie after this and see if we can align that, send you an invite.
Excellent.
Excellent.
Well, I appreciate it and it was good to meet you.
Yeah, good to meet you too.
And good to know that you're out there actively looking for more stuff.
If something doesn't come with this, then maybe we can refer some more leads your way.
Sounds good.
Okay, be well.
Take care.
All right.
Enjoy your conference.
Thanks.
Cheers and speak soon.
Thank you.

summary.action_items:
**Andrew Day**
Coordinate with Leslie to confirm her availability for a meeting with Stan Steinreich on Thursday morning (East Coast time, between 10:00 and 12:00), and send a calendar invite to Stan (10:27)
summary.overview:
- **Key Insight #1**: Stan Steinreich represents top players in home furnishings; his firm, Steinreich Communications, has 22 years of experience and operates 9 global offices with a focus on PR and social media. Important for leveraging relationships in the industry.

- **Key Insight #2**: Capital A serves both sell-side via Agencies Co marketplace and buy-side for agencies. Andrew Day highlighted a specific acquisition target: a small PR firm in Georgia led by a UK founder, focused on government/nonprofit sectors. Key point: client values vision and chemistry in a buyer.

- **Key Insight #3**: Acquisition criteria established by Stan: targets under $1M, desires strong leadership for post-acquisition continuity. Stresses reviewing P&L and operations early to avoid time wastage. Next step: Schedule an introductory call with the seller soon, aimed for Thursday morning.
summary.short_summary: Stan Steinreich, representing Steinreich Communications, and Andrew Day of Capital A convened to explore acquisition opportunities within the PR sector. They discussed a potential acquisition of a small PR firm in Georgia, led by a UK founder and specializing in government and nonprofit sectors, who is looking for a buyer that aligns with their vision. Stan detailed his acquisition criteria, favoring firms under $1 million with strong leadership for continuity post-acquisition, and emphasized the necessity of early review of financials and operations to streamline the process. The two agreed to arrange an introductory call for Thursday morning to discuss the opportunity further, with Andrew optimistic about coordinating schedules with the client. Both expressed interest in future collaborations beyond this transaction.
